scope: Posthoc explanatory metric geometry on old DEV archived-checkpoint and no-fit uniform-weight intervention only. Not qualification, selector input, fitting, or fresh confirmation.

definition.prediction: current + target_mean + coefficient @ output_basis.T; concatenate horizons 3 and 6
definition.affine_reference: For each counterfactual_group, affine span of actual-plan true future feature prototypes; one singular direction for S and three for R/D. Future information is evaluation-only.
definition.parallel_mse: Squared length of prediction-target residual projected into the centered prototype span, divided by total concatenated feature dimension.
definition.orthogonal_mse: Squared length orthogonal to that span, with the same denominator. The target lies in the span, so this is prediction distance to the affine prototype subspace.
definition.distance_classification: Nearest-prototype decisions depend only on parallel residual differences because the orthogonal distance is common to all prototypes. Correct classification can coexist with larger within-span error because classification only fixes a region, not distance.
definition.aggregation: Native K2 complete sets only plus full K3; R contributes two valid complete deletions per parent. Rows within a family are not independent.

limitations: The prototype span is determined by observed actual futures and must never be used as a causal retention score.
Only the two evaluated horizons and actual action plan enter this geometry; no other future behaviors are implied.
A small orthogonal residual does not imply physical validity, and a large residual can include feature variation unrelated to class identity.
This is descriptive posthoc decomposition; no new endpoint or qualification rule is introduced.
interpretation: For native complete K2 in R and D, uniform weighting improves nearest-prototype classification while raising total feature MSE. Mean error inside the prototype span decreases (R -0.0038823; D -0.0036206), but orthogonal error increases more (R +0.0230174; D +0.0218864). The conflict is thus mainly orthogonal prediction error, not a worsened class-relevant direction on average.

The same decomposition holds in every R/D native-complete-K2 salience condition: parallel MSE improves and orthogonal MSE worsens. For salient-useful D specifically, accuracy changes from 0.59375 to 0.9479166666666666, parallel MSE by -0.002670394820906731, and orthogonal MSE by 0.04280281601657381.

Among native K2 rows changing from wrong to correct, 103/137 R rows and 35/42 D rows nevertheless have higher total MSE. In these conflict subsets, mean parallel changes are -0.0061695 and -0.0034365; orthogonal changes are +0.0395729 and +0.0503491. Orthogonal increase exceeds parallel increase in 100/103 and 33/35 rows, respectively.

R full-K3 classification also improves (73.264% to 94.097%), with MSE +0.0298465; orthogonal change +0.0250076 is about 83.8% of the mean MSE increase, while parallel change +0.0048389 also worsens. Correct classification fixes a Voronoi region, not prediction magnitude within it.

D full-K3 and S full-K3 do not show the same overall classification-versus-MSE conflict: both classification and MSE worsen. S K3 has parallel +0.0458578 and orthogonal +0.0165364; about 73.5% of its mean MSE degradation lies along the prototype direction. Uniform weighting therefore does not solve S K3, even at the class-relevant geometric level.
S native-complete-K2 keeps accuracy 93.75% and slightly improves MSE: parallel -0.0030260 outweighs orthogonal +0.0017607.

Orthogonal error is invisible to this fixed prototype classifier, but it remains genuine feature-prediction error under the frozen proposal metric. These results do not establish that MSE is wrong, do not justify replacing qualification with projected loss after seeing results, and do not prove that the ignored directions are irrelevant to other futures.
